title: Slip-stitch mosaic lap throw
subtitle: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw in a two-colour slip-stitch mosaic on 4 mm needles.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw worked flat in a two-colour slip-stitch mosaic pattern on 4 mm needles. Only one colour is worked per row; the other is slipped. The result is a geometric colour pattern without stranding. About 400 g of each DK colour.
sourceNotes: Barbara Walker's A Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1968), §Mosaic Patterns, establishes slip-stitch mosaic as a public-domain technique for two-colour geometric fabric without stranding. Slip-stitch colourwork is also described in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 12th series (1896), §Slip Stitch Patterns.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in mosaic pattern on 4 mm needles. Mosaic fabric is taller per row than stocking stitch.

glossaryTerms.definition: A slip-stitch colourwork technique where only one colour is used per row. Stitches of the second colour are slipped (not knitted) and picked up in the next same-colour row. The floats of the slipped stitches are hidden behind the work. Produces two-colour geometric patterns without the complexity of stranded colourwork.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 4 mm needles in a two-colour
mosaic knitting
pattern, finishing at 100 cm wide by 120 cm long.

Only one colour is active per row; the other colour's stitches are slipped purlwise with yarn in back on RS rows and yarn in front on WS rows. This avoids any stranding tension issues while still producing a geometric two-colour surface. The pattern used here is a simple eight-stitch, eight-row geometric repeat (offset squares). The two colours are changed every two rows at the right edge. Budget about 400 g of each colour (about 880 m / 960 yards per colour) of DK. Buy in matched dye lots within each colour.
What you need

items.name: Yarn A (dark)
items.qty: 400 g (about 880 m / 960 yards) of DK in a dark or strong colour

items.name: Yarn B (light)
items.qty: 400 g of DK in a contrasting light or neutral colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 120 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm in mosaic pattern. Mosaic fabric has more rows per 10 cm than stocking stitch because slipped stitches are taller. Swatch the full eight-row repeat in both colours for at least 12 cm before casting on; the mosaic fabric cannot be measured from a single-colour swatch.
If your row gauge is 40 rows per 10 cm instead of 44, the same row count produces the throw about 12 cm longer. Measure by tape; 120 cm is the target.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on

Using Yarn A and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 220 stitches (a multiple of 8, plus 4 edge stitches; the mosaic repeat is 8 stitches). Long-tail tail: (4 × 220) / 10 + 15 = 88 + 15 = 103 cm. Measure 120 cm.
Body (8-row, 8-stitch repeat)
With Yarn A, Row 1 (RS): k2, *k4, sl1wyb, k1, sl1wyb, k1; rep from * to last 2 sts, k2.
With Yarn A, Row 2 (WS): k2, *k4, sl1wyf, k1, sl1wyf, k1; rep from * to last 2 sts, k2.
Change to Yarn B. With Yarn B, Row 3 (RS): k2, *sl1wyb, k1, sl1wyb, k1, sl1wyb, k3; rep from * to last 2 sts, k2.
With Yarn B, Row 4 (WS): k2, *sl1wyf, k1, sl1wyf, k1, sl1wyf, k3; rep from * to last 2 sts, k2.

Continue the 8-row repeat, alternating Yarn A and Yarn B every 2 rows, until the throw measures 120 cm. When you set this aside, note the row number within the repeat and which colour is on the needle.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 264 (about 60 cm): count across. You should have 220 stitches. Mosaic never increases or decreases stitch count. At row 525 (about 119 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults

Pattern shifting sideways: the slip placement was off by one stitch on a RS row. The slipped stitches must align exactly above the slipped stitches of the previous same-colour RS row. After each RS row, check that the slipped columns are vertically aligned with those below.

Tight floats pulling in the width: slipped stitches were pulled tight. Keep slipped stitches spread on the right needle before completing them, so the float behind lies loose enough that it cannot be seen from the front.
Cast-off
Cast off knitwise with Yarn A (or whichever colour is active at 120 cm), with a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in all yarn-change ends along the right edge. A light block will even out the mosaic fabric.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

From a simple mosaic, try a longer repeat next: 16 rows or 24 rows. Or try stranded colourwork: the same two-colour concept, but both yarns are carried across each row. The fabric is denser and less stretchy.
